Theek hai bhai, araam se, ekdum dheere-dheere. Sochiye,
 GitHub Actions ka runner ek naya sa, saaf Ubuntu machine hai. 
 Ab Step one — sabse pehle aapka source code runner tak lana padta hai. Jaise: actions/checkout use karke. 
 Iska matlab tumhara code runner ke paas aa gaya. Agar checkout nahi karoge,
  to baad ke steps ke paas dekhne ke liye kuch hoga hi nahi. Step two.
  Ab runner ko samjhana padta hai ki kaunsa environment chahiye. Jaise Node.js, Java, ya Python.
   Hum respective setup action use karte hain. Iske baad runner aapka project chalane ke liye tayyar ho jata hai. 
   Step three fir dependencies restore ya install hoti hain. Jaise Node mein 'npm ci', Java mein 'mvn install',
    yahin par aksar cache ka fayda hota hai— jaldi restore ho jaati hain. Step four do cheezein hain. 
    Pehle unit tests chalate hain, jaise 'npm test'. Agar ye fail hue to aksar pipeline ruk jaati hai.
     Fir SonarQube analysis hota hai jo bugs, security issues, code smells jaise cheezein scan karta hai. 
     Agar aapka SonarQube self-hosted hai, to runner us server tak pohonch sakta ho aur token properly configured ho
     . Step five mein application build karte hain, jaise 'npm run build' ya equivalent. Output jaise 'dist/' 
     folder ya 'app.jar' ban jaata hai. Step six, agar container deploy karna hai to Docker image build hoti hai. 
     Jaise 'docker build -t myapp:1.0 . Step seven pe uss image ko Trivy se security scan karte hain. 
     Agar high ya critical vulnerabilities milti hain, to team ke hisaab se pipeline fail bhi ho sakti hai.
      Step eight, sab clear ho gaya to image Azure Container Registry (ACR) mein push kar dete hain, usually proper 
Azure login ya OIDC setup ke saath. 
Aur phir wahi image deployment ke liye ready ho jaati hai
